title: A Dynamic Decomposition Strategy for the MOEA/D With Proven Performance Guarantees
claim: Classic benchmark objective values are densely packed, while a monotonic distortion leaves large gaps between points, though the Pareto front is unchanged.
layout: 2 panels side by side, each with axes and diagonal point lines; captions below
description: Two side-by-side scatter sketches of objective space. Panel (a), the original LOTZ benchmark, has axes L(x) horizontal and T(x) vertical, with ticks n-2 and n. Dense dotted diagonal lines of blue points fill the triangle under an outermost orange diagonal line, which is the Pareto front from (0,n) to (n,0). Panel (b), the monotonically distorted version, has axes u(L(x)) and v(T(x)). It has the same diagonal structure, but the points are sparse and unevenly spaced. The gaps widen toward the upper right, and the points crowd near the origin. The orange Pareto-front points are far apart. Black arrowed axes frame each panel. Captions (a) and (b) explain each panel. The eye goes first to the orange line and then to the blue stripes.
caption: A graphical sketch of the LeadingOnesTrailingZeros (\lotz) [ref] benchmark ([ref]) and its monotonically distorted version [ref] ([ref]). The details are given in [ref]. The orange points on the outmost line denote the Pareto front of the respective benchmark. The other blue points denote other objective values that are not Pareto optima.
abstract: The MOEA/D is one of the most successful multi-objective evolutionary algorithms. It operates by decomposing the optimization problem into single-objective subproblems, which are then solved in a co-evolutionary manner. The performance of the MOEA/D depends critically on this decomposition. In this work, we propose a novel way to adjust this decomposition on the fly, for the case of discrete bi-objective optimization. Different from all previous works in this direction, we support our new algorithm with a proven performance guarantee. This is the first work that rigorously proves the runtime of a dynamic multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. For monotonic distortions of the simple LOTZ benchmark, it is known that classic decompositions leave large holes in the Pareto front, making it very hard for the MOEA/D to cover the entire Pareto front. In contrast, we prove that our self-adjusting MOEA/D solves all these LOTZ problems in an expected number of $O(n^4)$ function evaluations. This relatively low runtime as well as the details of our mathematical proof show that the dynamic decomposition strategy indeed evolves a decomposition adjusted to each of these problem instances.
